title: List Collections Request
description: Experimental (media_buy.collection_catalog), added in AdCP 3.3. Read the selling agent's catalog of collection cards: look up specific collections by key, or browse with filters and pages. Returns the same core/response-collection.json copies, under the same authority rules, as include_collections on product and proposal reads, and never returns products. Not to be confused with list_collection_lists, which lists buyer-owned collection targeting lists on a governance agent. Side-effect free: the call never provisions an account. It is the bootstrap and repair read for collection_card.* and collection_catalog.bulk_change webhooks, which are registered only through sync_accounts notification_configs; the request takes no push_notification_config, so a call never creates a subscription. Sellers implementing it MUST list media_buy.collection_catalog and media_buy.collection_cards in experimental_features. A seller MUST NOT serve this task to a caller whose adcp_version is below 3.3; it fails the request with UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE.
x-tool-summary: List a seller's collection cards (shows, creators, podcasts) by key or with filters, without products.

idempotency_key.description: Optional replay key accepted uniformly on read calls.

account.description: Optional account scope. Only the set of collections visible to the caller may vary by account; the content of a copy for a given (publisher_domain, collection_id) never does. Without account the response is cache_scope public.

collections.description: Optional selectors, the same shape as a product's collections, so a buyer can pass a product's selectors through unchanged. A selector with collection_ids is a key lookup; a selector with only publisher_domain means every collection of that publisher that this seller represents. At most 100 collection_ids in total across all selectors; sellers reject more with VALIDATION_ERROR. A key that is unknown or not visible to the caller is omitted from the response without a per-key error. Omit to browse the whole catalog.

filters.description: Optional filters, applied with the selectors before pagination. Values within one filter are alternatives (OR); different filters combine with AND. Filters run on the seller's copy, so a match on genre, status, talent or kind is a discovery hint: buyers confirm those fields against the publisher's adagents.json before relying on them for suitability. A seller that cannot apply a filter it receives fails the request with VALIDATION_ERROR and never returns a broader result.

kinds.description: Include only collections of these kinds. Same semantics as kinds in collection/collection-list-filters.json.

genres_include.description: Include only collections with any of these genres; collections without genre metadata are excluded. Values are interpreted against genre_taxonomy when present. Same semantics as in collection/collection-list-filters.json.

genres_exclude.description: Exclude collections tagged with any of these genres, applied after genres_include. Values are interpreted against genre_taxonomy when present.

genre_taxonomy.description: Taxonomy for genre filter values. When present, genres_include and genres_exclude values are taxonomy IDs.

statuses.description: Include only collections with any of these statuses.

languages.description: Include only collections whose language matches any of these BCP 47 language ranges under RFC 4647 basic filtering, compared case-insensitively: 'en' matches 'en' and 'en-US', but 'en-US' does not match 'en'.

talent.description: Include only collections with a talent entry whose brand_ref matches any of these brands. Only domain and brand_id are compared, as on talent; brand_id omitted matches any brand_ref at that domain.

platforms.description: Include only collections with a distribution entry whose publisher_domain is any of these domains.

name_contains.description: Include only collections whose name contains this string, compared case-insensitively.

pagination.description: Cursor pagination (default 50, maximum 100 per page). The cursor is outside the collections_version scope. Order is seller-defined and stable within one collections_version; if a later page returns a different collections_version, restart from the first page.

if_collections_version.description: Opaque collections_version from a prior list_collections response for the same scope: the canonicalized collections selectors and filters (arrays compared as sets, pagination.cursor excluded), plus account identity when that response's cache_scope was account. When it matches, the seller returns outcome unchanged without collections. A token from a different scope is a mismatch and gets a full listed response. Unrelated to feed_version and wholesale_feed_version. A webhook-fed mirror repairing after a gap sends its last applied version, never a newer webhook version.
